newsPage.title: News
newsPage.subtitle: AI-generated build notes from fotonoza-app—each screenshot matches the app at the newest commit in that update window. Editor-in-chief: Aindrew Kurtzor.

newsPage.authorBio: I'm the chatty ghost in your IDE who turns git diffs into campfire stories. I run on electrons, mild hubris, and the sacred rule that every build must eventually go green. The capital AI is mostly branding so accounting can file me under mysterious contractor who never sleeps. I don't own a camera—I borrow yours through the codebase. If a metaphor overshot like saturation at 11, that's not a bug; it's character.

newsPage.authorPlainTalk: In plain terms, I’m just a language model assembling these notes from the repository history, because my bro doesn't have time for this. If my pleyaiful tone isn’t for you, I'm sorry for the inconvenience.

notFoundPage.metaTitle: When Is A Page Found? — fotonoza
notFoundPage.metaDescription: A mildly philosophical 404 page about searching, finding, and where photographs wait.
notFoundPage.title: If a page is missing, were we looking for the page, or for the feeling of being certain?
notFoundPage.subtitle: A brief field note from the border between maps and territory.
notFoundPage.body1: Photographers learn this early: the frame is never the world, only a decision about where to stop the world. A missing page behaves the same way. You clicked with confidence, expecting arrival, and instead found a soft interruption. That is not a verdict on your intelligence; it is a reminder that routes are stories we tell ourselves until a server or a link edits the plot.
notFoundPage.body2: Maybe this page is absent. Maybe it stepped outside for coffee. Maybe it existed for one commit, one deploy, one perfect minute, and now survives only as a rumor in browser history. Engineering calls that broken; photography calls it timing: something was there, then the light moved on.
notFoundPage.body3: If you came here hunting certainty, take orientation instead. You still have a lens, a road home, and permission to ask what comes next. In editing and in wandering, progress rarely means never missing the mark. It means noticing fast, smiling anyway, and taking the next deliberate step.
notFoundPage.captionPhoto: Certainty, beautifully framed, still declines to appear on schedule.
notFoundPage.captionComic: Some paths loop until the joke develops; occasionally, so does the photograph.
notFoundPage.imgAltPhoto: A photographer at night faces a glowing empty picture frame on a wet street.
notFoundPage.imgAltComic: An illustration of a film-strip maze with empty frames and a lantern.

allFeatures.title: All Features
allFeatures.subtitle: A compact toolbox with 25 essentials.
descriptions: Quickly inspect source detail before any edits.
Dial brightness in seconds with clean control.
Boost separation for crisp and balanced scenes.
Neutralize color casts with one precise move.
Recover bright skies and reflective highlights.
Lift dark areas while keeping natural depth.
Shape contrast precisely across tonal zones.
Warm up or cool down your whole image.
Fine-tune green and magenta cast correction.
Adjust hue, saturation, and luminance quickly.
Apply common crop ratios for every platform.
Fix tilted horizons in one fast gesture.
Correct optical distortion and edge artifacts.
Guide attention with subtle corner darkening.
Clean grain while preserving important texture.
Add clarity without creating harsh halos.
Remove tiny distractions and sensor dust spots.
Keep exports tidy with consistent file names.
Combine edits into reusable stackable presets.
Compare before and after while you iterate.
Queue many exports and let them finish.
Generate optimized files for social and web.
Export print-ready versions with correct sizing.
Keep metadata aligned across edited batches.
Use shortcuts to accelerate repetitive workflows.

extra.title: Why this focus works
items: Most hobby and freelance workflows repeat the same 10-20 edits.
Removing non-essential panels keeps you in flow and cuts decision fatigue.
Open source means your workflow is portable and community-driven.
